jobs.title: Vice President, Health Information and Technology
jobs.description:
Texas Health Action (THA) is a community-informed non-profit organization dedicated to providing access to culturally affirming, quality health services in a safe and supportive environment, with expertise in serving LGBTQIA+ people and those impacted by HIV. Kind Clinic proudly serves Texas with four vibrant locations: two in Austin, one in San Antonio, and another in Dallas plus virtual care services available to all residents across Texas. Bolstered by Waterloo Counseling Center and a passionate team of over 250 dedicated employees and volunteers, THA is at the forefront of promoting healthcare equity and accessibility throughout the state. Read more about THA here: http://texashealthaction.org.

The Vice President, Health Information & Technology
provides senior level leadership for the organization's Information Technology (IT)
and Health Information Management (HIM)
functions, including clinical applications, data systems, interoperability, security, and information/data governance. This role is responsible for the technology and information system infrastructure of the organization and its future direction.

This role serves as a strategic partner to the CEO
, translating organizational goals into a cohesive technology and data strategy and ensuring disciplined execution across infrastructure, clinical systems, analytics, and compliance. The VP is accountable for aligning technology investments with patient care and experience, operational excellence, regulatory requirements, and long-term organizational growth.

Core Functions

Senior Leadership & Strategy

Serve as the senior most leader for IT, clinical applications, data, and information management and security functions.
Partner with the CEO and executive team to develop and maintain a multi-year technology and data strategy aligned with organizational priorities
Translate organization strategy into clear roadmaps, budgets, and operational plans for technology and information systems.
Advise executive leadership on emerging technology, digital health trends, and data capabilities relevant to healthcare delivery.
Develop budgets in collaboration with IT and HIM leaders, advise on technology investments to support technology and information system strategy and organization growth.
Ensure the security, reliability, capability, and scalability of our information systems and technology to execute our mission.

Technology & Infrastructure Oversight

Oversee all IT operations including:
Network and infrastructure
End-user systems and support
Vendor and contract management
Cybersecurity and risk management
Ensure technology platforms are scalable, reliable, secure, and cost-effective.

Clinical Applications & Health Information Management

Provide senior level oversight for:
Electronic Health Record (EHR) and other clinical systems
Practice management and revenue cycle technologies
Telehealth platforms
Clinical workflows and optimization
Partner with clinical and operational leaders to ensure systems support high-quality, patient-centered care.
Oversee health information governance, including data quality, documentation standards, and lifecycle management.

Data, Analytics & Reporting

Lead development of enterprise data capabilities, including:
Reporting and dashboards
Quality, outcomes, and compliance reporting
Population health and performance analytics
Ensure data is accurate, accessible, secure, and actionable for leadership, clinical teams, and external reporting.

Compliance, Security & Risk

Ensure compliance with all applicable regulations (e.g., HIPAA, HITECH, state and federal reporting requirements).
Oversee cybersecurity strategy, incident response planning, and privacy safeguards.
Collaborate with compliance and legal functions on audits and risk mitigation.
Serve as the organization's security officer

Team Leadership & Culture

Directly manage IT and HIM leaders and build a high-performing, mission-aligned team.
Clarify roles, expectations, and accountability across technical and clinical application teams.
Foster collaboration between technology staff and teams of various departments across the organization.

Compensation

Based on the position's duties and requirements, this role has a starting annual salary of $147,721.60. The initial salary will be determined by the selected candidate's qualifications and relevant experience.

Requirements

Education and/or Licensure

Required

Bachelor's degree in Information Systems, Healthcare Administration, Business, Computer Science, or a related field.

Preferred

Master's degree (MHA, MBA, MPH, MS in Health Informatics or Information Systems).
Relevant certifications (e.g., CHCIO, PMP, CAHIMS, CPDHTS, CPHIMS, CISSP) a plus but not required.

Experience

10+ years of progressive leadership experience in healthcare IT, health information systems, or digital health. 5+ years in a senior leadership role (Director, Senior Director, or VP level).
Demonstrated experience overseeing: EHR and clinical systems, IT infrastructure and security, and data and reporting in a healthcare environment
Experience translating organizational strategy into technology roadmaps and operational execution.
Strong vendor management and budget oversight experience.
Experience in nonprofit healthcare, community health, public health, or complex regulated environments strongly preferred.

Knowledge Skills and Abilities

Must have basic PC skills that include a combination of working in a Windows Operating System and Microsoft Outlook, Word, and Excel
Understands the importance of maintaining confidentiality; able to maintain confidentiality under HIPAA standards
Must have the ability to exercise a high degree of diplomacy and tact; excellent customer services and interpersonal communication skills; Cultural sensitivity and demonstrated ability to work with diverse people groups
Well-developed verbal and written communication skills in English; Additional language abilities desirable. Ability to work well under pressure with minimal supervision.
Ability to effectively interact with persons of widely diverse roles, backgrounds, cultures, and socio-economic classes, those in crises or resistant or negative toward organizations
Ability to apply time management practices to prioritize, schedule and complete work effectively to comply with mandated policies and deadlines.
Ability to work on multiple tasks or parts of tasks simultaneously to ensure timely completion of work activities.
Must be able to work productively with other departments and employees
Ability to work with professionals from various partners and organizations
Usually works forty (40) hours per week, some weekends may be required
Must be able to multi-task, prioritize with strong time management skills.
Exceptional follow through on tasks and assignments

Physical Requirements/Environmental Conditions

Perform the following with or without reasonable accommodations:
Ability to express and exchange ideas via spoken word during activities in which they must convey detail or important spoken instructions to others accurately, sometimes quickly and loudly.
Hearing to perceive the nature of sound with no less than 40 db loss @ Hz, 1000 Hz, and 2000 Hz with or without correction; ability to perceive detailed information orally and make fine discriminations in sound.
Perform repetitive motions with wrists, hands, and fingers. Individual must be able to exert up to 12 pounds of force occasionally and to be able to lift, carry, push, pull, or otherwise move objects.
Work requires a minimum standard of visual acuity with or without correction that will enable people in the role to complete administrative and clerical tasks, as well as inspect and analyze
Must be able to work and concentrate amidst distractions such as noise, conversation, and foot traffic; ability to handle interruptions often and be able to move from one task to another
While worker may possibly be subjected to temperature changes, the worker is generally not substantially exposed to adverse environmental conditions as the work is predominantly inside

Benefits

Health Care Plan (Medical, Dental & Vision)
Retirement Plan (403b)
Life Insurance (Basic, Voluntary & AD&D)
Paid Time Off (Vacation, Sick & Holidays)
Short-Term & Long-Term Disability
Training & Development
Parental Leave
Longevity Pay

Applicant Information

Submitting official transcripts, diplomas, certifications and licenses may be required prior to final offer. Unofficial transcripts and copies of other relevant documents may be attached to the application for consideration in advance.
Information regarding employment history as it relates to the qualifications of the position may be needed for employment verification.
The applicant selected for employment is subject to a pre-employment background check. A history of conviction may not automatically disqualify an applicant. Applicants with a history of conviction may be considered on a case-by-case basis, after individualized assessment of factors including the nature of the conviction, the job duties and responsibilities, the length of time since the conviction, and evidence of mitigation or rehabilitation. If required for the position, a physical, motor vehicle record evaluation, and additional background checks may be conducted.

EEO Statement:

We do not discriminate based upon race, religion, color, national origin, gender (including pregnancy, childbirth, or related medical conditions), sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, age, status as a protected veteran, status as an individual with a disability, or other applicable legally protected characteristics.

Company Description
Helios Insurance Services, Inc. operates as a wholesale insurance provider with a focus on Property & Casualty products. The company partners with insurance carriers and retail agencies to deliver specialized coverage solutions across diverse markets. Its wholesale model enables tailored risk management offerings and flexible underwriting options for clients. Professionals joining Helios can expect to work in a dynamic environment focused on innovation, service quality, and long-term industry relationships.
Role Description
The Vice President of Technology is a full-time, remote leadership role responsible for overseeing all technology initiatives at Helios Insurance Services, Inc. This position guides the development and execution of the IT strategy to support business goals in the wholesale Property & Casualty insurance space. Day-to-day responsibilities include managing technology teams, prioritizing and delivering IT projects, and ensuring systems are secure, scalable, and aligned with regulatory and industry standards. The role involves collaborating with executive leadership to drive strategic planning, evaluating emerging technologies, and optimizing core platforms and integrations. The Vice President of Technology also establishes performance metrics, manages vendor relationships, and promotes continuous improvement in processes, data quality, and user experience.
Qualifications

Strong Information Technology leadership experience, including oversight of infrastructure, applications, and security.
Demonstrated IT Strategy and Strategic Planning skills to align technology initiatives with business priorities.
Proven Project Management capabilities, including leading cross-functional projects and managing timelines, budgets, and resources.
Advanced Analytical Skills for evaluating technology performance, risk, and opportunities, and for data-driven decision-making.
Experience in the insurance industry, preferably Property & Casualty or wholesale insurance, is highly beneficial.
Track record of building and mentoring high-performing technology teams in a remote or distributed environment.
Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to collaborate effectively at all organizational levels.
Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, Engineering, or a related field; advanced degree or relevant certifications (e.g., PMP, CISSP, ITIL) are a plus.

jobs.title: Sr IT Director II
jobs.description:
Job Description

The Senior IT Director II, Operations Delivery & Reliability is a senior leadership role accountable for the platforms on which the enterprise builds, hosts, and runs software — and for the controls, lifecycle, and quality disciplines that keep the technology estate reliable, compliant, and current. The role owns Tower 4 (Application & Developer Platforms) and Tower 5 (Service Reliability & Technology Stewardship) of the IT Infrastructure Services operating model. This Level II Senior Director leads other director- and senior-manager-level leaders across application hosting and platform engineering, integration, DevOps and automation, observability, and the enterprise service-management, configuration, asset, lifecycle, and technology-controls functions.

This role pairs a build-and-run platform mandate with an independent stewardship mandate: enabling development teams to deliver software quickly and safely, while governing the change, incident, configuration, compliance, and lifecycle disciplines that protect service quality across every tower. The successful candidate is equally comfortable commanding a Sev-1 major-incident bridge, setting the roadmap for the enterprise ITSM and observability platforms, and briefing executive leadership on reliability, technical-debt, and license-compliance posture.

Key Responsibilities

Tower 4 — Application & Developer Platforms (build, host, and run software)

Own the application hosting and platform estate — web, database, and big-data hosting, PaaS, and middleware — ensuring the platforms that host enterprise software are secure, performant, and scalable.
Own support for SaaS and third-party applications, providing consistent operational ownership, vendor coordination, and service levels across the third-party application portfolio.
Own enterprise integration and batch services — APIs, messaging, ETL/ELT, and scheduled batch processing — as the connective tissue between applications and data.
Own the DevOps and CI/CD toolchain and the platform-engineering and automation function, giving delivery teams self-service pipelines, infrastructure-as-code, and release automation to build, test, and ship software safely and quickly.
Own the enterprise GenAI platform — the shared, governed foundation for AI-enabled capabilities (model access, orchestration, and guardrails) — in partnership with the Office of the CTO on AI governance (AI TRiSM).
Own the observability platform — enterprise monitoring, logging, tracing, and telemetry — providing the signal that underpins reliability, capacity, and performance decisions across all towers.

Tower 5 — Service Reliability & Technology Stewardship (controls, lifecycle, and quality)

Own the enterprise ITSM platform (e.g., ServiceNow) as the system of record for IT service management, including its health, roadmap, and adoption across all towers and affiliate entities.
Own the core service-management processes — incident, problem, and change management — and lead the Major Incident Management function, including Sev-1/Sev-2 command, executive communications, and post-incident review.
Own configuration management and the CMDB, maintaining accurate, trusted service and asset relationships that underpin change, incident, and impact analysis.
Own IT asset and software license management — hardware and software inventory, entitlement and true-up positioning, and license compliance — in partnership with FinOps and vendor management on cost and renewal exposure.
Own the technology-lifecycle function — currency, end-of-life / end-of-support tracking, and remediation planning — to keep the estate supportable and reduce technical debt and risk.
Coordinate the technology-controls response for compliance, audit, and vulnerability management — evidence, control attestation, and remediation — partnering with Information Security and Internal Audit / Risk. (This role coordinates and remediates technology controls; it does not replace second-line security or audit functions.)
Own workforce IAM operations — joiner/mover/leaver provisioning, access-request fulfillment, and periodic access certification — partnering with the infrastructure towers that own the underlying identity infrastructure (Active Directory, DNS, federation) and with Information Security on IAM policy.

Cross-Tower Leadership, Sourcing & Governance

Lead and develop director- and senior-manager-level leaders across both towers; set clear accountability, coach for performance, and build bench strength.
Govern the internal-versus-partner-delivered sourcing mix: keep architecture, standards, platform ownership, and incident/change leadership internal, and direct commodity run, application support, and after-hours coverage to delivery partners under clear SLA and performance governance.
Own and mature the tower-level KPI/scorecard — platform availability and SLO attainment, MTTR, change success rate, major-incident frequency, CMDB accuracy, license-compliance position, and vulnerability-remediation SLA — and use the data to drive investment, staffing, and process decisions.
Partner with Finance and the Office of the CTO (Tower 6) on TBM cost pools and unit economics for these towers (e.g., cost per application, per pipeline, per license), supporting the transition from showback to chargeback.
Represent Operations Delivery & Reliability in the Architecture Review Board, Change Advisory Board, and Risk & Resilience Committee, and in executive and leadership forums, preparing clear, data-backed materials and recommendations.
Champion continuous improvement across both towers — modeling a culture of accountability and disciplined execution, and applying ITIL 4 continual-improvement and Lean practices.

Qualifications

7+ years of progressive IT leadership experience, with direct experience in application platforms / platform engineering and/or IT service management and service reliability within a complex, matrixed organization.
Prior experience managing and leading other director-level or senior-manager-level technical leaders.
Hands-on depth in several of: application hosting (web/database/middleware), PaaS, enterprise integration / APIs and batch, DevOps / CI-CD and automation, observability/monitoring, and cloud-native application platforms.
Strong ITSM/ITIL foundation — incident, problem, change, configuration, and service-level management — with ServiceNow platform ownership experience strongly preferred; ITIL 4 certification a plus.
Demonstrated experience leading Major Incident Management (Sev-1 command) and running structured problem- and post-incident-review processes.
Experience with IT asset and software license management, technology lifecycle / currency management, and coordinating compliance, audit, and vulnerability remediation with security and audit partners.
Familiarity with IAM operations (joiner/mover/leaver provisioning, access certification) and its interplay with identity infrastructure and information security.
Exposure to GenAI platform enablement and AI governance (AI TRiSM) is a plus.
Demonstrated experience managing partner-delivered / outsourced application support and run operations, including SLA and performance governance; managed-services transition experience a strong plus.
Proven experience translating strategy into an execution roadmap, with strong business and financial acumen; TBM/FinOps familiarity a plus.
Excellent executive presence, written and verbal communication, and stakeholder-management skills, with the ability to influence senior leaders.
Experience with Lean / continuous-improvement methodologies (e.g., Lean Six Sigma) is a plus.

Preferred Qualifications

10+ years of progressive IT leadership experience, with direct experience in application platforms / platform engineering and/or IT service management and service reliability within a complex, matrixed organization.

Required Management Experience

5+ years direct supervisory/management experience

Required Education

Bachelor's degree in a related field or equivalent experience; Master's degree (MBA) and/or relevant certifications (ITIL 4, PMP) preferred.

General Physical Demands

Sedentary work: Exerting up to 10 pounds of force occasionally to move objects. Jobs are sedentary if traversing activities are required.

Physical/Environmental Activities

Must be able to travel to multiple locations for work (i.e. travel to attend meetings, events, conferences).

May be exposed to outdoor weather conditions of cold, heat, wet, and humidity. May be exposed to outdoor or warehouse conditions of loud noises, vibration, fumes, dust, odors, and mists. Must be able to ascend and descend ladders, stairs, or other equipment.

What We Offer

As a Florida Blue employee, you will be at the heart of GuideWell’s vision – to lead the nation in transforming health through compassionate, connected, and technology-enabled care that delivers personalized value and empowered living.

To support your wellbeing, comprehensive benefits are offered. As an employee, you will have access to:

Leave programs to support personal circumstances;
Retirement Savings Plan including employer match;
Paid time off, volunteer time off, 10 holidays and 2 well-being days;
Additional voluntary benefits available; and
A comprehensive wellness program

Employee benefits are designed to align with federal and state employment laws. Benefits may vary based on the state in which work is performed. Benefits for intern, part-time and seasonal employees may differ.

To support your financial wellbeing, we offer competitive pay as well as opportunities for incentive or commission compensation. We also conduct regular annual reviews with pay for performance considerations for base pay increases.

$180,000 - $292,500

Typical Annualized Hiring Range:

Final pay will be determined with consideration of market competitiveness, internal equity, and the job-related knowledge, skills, training, and experience you bring.

jobs.title: Program Manager - Research Security Program
jobs.description:
TS/SCI

Overview

This position supports the IRMPO as a planning authority and expert advisor for formalizing and maturing the Department Research Security Program in compliance with National Security Presidential Memorandum-33 (NSPM-33, United States Government-Supported Research and Development National Security Policy), the Creating Helpful Incentives to Produce Semiconductors (CHIPS) and Science Act, and other research security policies, regulations, and statutes.

Background

The Insider Risk Management Program Office (IRMPO), a component of the Deputy Assistant Secretary for Security, Insider Risk and Continuity (OSIRC) serves to mitigate the risk to personnel, facilities, property, information, and assets through increased initiatives in various security fields via issuance of U.S. Department of Commerce-wide security policies and the application of a multi-disciplined security programs extending from the Headquarters to the operating units. IRMPO plans and implements policies by developing procedures and delivering a wide range of services for the Office of the Secretary and other nationwide Departmental bureaus.

Responsibilities

Although other general duties within the scope of the position may be assigned, primary responsibilities include:

Review and assess Research Security Program Plans and procedures.
Develop and manage the content for a Research Security Awareness Training program for Department of Commerce employees and associates.
Work with staff to develop a more comprehensive Research Security compliance program.
Assist in preparation of requested materials for the Department’s Research Security and Insider Risk mission.
Assist in development of policies and guidance related to the Department’s Research Security and Insider Risk mission.
Assist in staffing and tracking Interagency, Task Force(s), and National Security Council taskings.
Attend interagency and internal Research Security and Insider Risk working groups as may be required.
Evaluate the efficiency and effectiveness of Research Security Programs, make recommendations for improvement, and implement approved initiatives.

Qualifications

Approximately eight years of relevant professional experience, including approximately four years of Research Security experience.

Federal Research Security experience at the Department/Agency headquarters level is preferred.
Experience in a scientific or education research environment.
Four years of supervisory experience preferred.
Demonstrated ability to communicate clearly, concisely, and effectively with a variety of audiences, both verbally and in writing.
Exceptional writing skills and proficiency with Microsoft 365 applications; this is a writing-intensive position.

Security Clearance: Top Secret (TS) security clearance with SCI crossover eligibility (not simply SCI eligible). This requires an in-scope background investigation and either currently SCI-indoc’d or read out of SCI within the past 23 months.

Education

Bachelor of Science (BS) degree in a scientific, technical, or engineering discipline
required. Candidates with a Bachelor of Arts (BA) degree may qualify with four additional years of relevant professional experience, for a total of at least 12 years of relevant experience. Master’s degree preferred.

Location and Work Hours

Full-time on-site at U.S. Department of Commerce Headquarters, 1401 Constitution Avenue NW, Washington, DC.

The Contracting Officer’s Representative, under limited circumstances (e.g., COVID/Hazardous Weather Days/Public Transportation Issues), may approve situational telework.

This position requires occasional travel to the Mount Weather Emergency Operations Center in Mount Weather, Virginia, including the ability to report to the facility on short notice when operational needs require. Employees are responsible for reliable transportation to and from the facility, as transportation is not provided by AES, and must be able to meet all applicable requirements for access to the facility and its grounds.

Compensation

Salary Range:
$132,870 – $176,000 annually

Compensation will be commensurate with the selected candidate's qualifications, relevant experience, and overall fit for the position.

Continuing Education Assistance

US citizenship may be a prerequisite for certain roles.

jobs.title: Senior Manager - IT Audit
jobs.description:
Job Description

Our Internal Audit Group is a worldwide function with 400+ team members and offices across nine countries within American Express. Our mission is to protect and enhance organizational value by providing independent, objective, risk-based assurance, advisory services and to influence the way the company manages risk.

We are committed to growing our audit staff significantly as we continue to expand and enhance the Internal Audit Group. Our assurance and risk professionals have diverse backgrounds including internal controls, consumer compliance, technology, operational risk, financial accounting, data analytics, and banking operations. Our audit teams align to key risk areas and business units to ensure IAG can provide comprehensive and risk-based audit coverage. In addition, IAG has a Professional Practices group responsible for managing audit operations, quality, and standards; regulatory relations; reporting; training and professional development; and key internal capabilities and technologies.

About The Role

Our Internal Audit group is seeking an eager Senior Manager - IT Audit in New York City, Phoenix, AZ, Charlotte, NC or Sandy, UT. This role will audit technology and application controls integrated into first-line and second-line business processes within an integrated audit with other audit disciplines. The ideal candidate will have strong problem- solving skills, excellent attention to detail, and the ability to communicate audit results effectively.

Responsibilities

Act as an Auditor in Charge (AIC) on more complex audits and/or lead multiple simultaneous low-risk audits, executing and managing the audit engagement end-to-end, planning audit projects, defining objectives and scope, and coordinating with control groups and external auditors to ensure effective execution; conduct L1 reviews
Analyze/review audit results and documentation to evaluate effectiveness and efficiency, synthesizing audit findings
Lead audit client meetings and walkthroughs
Develop test steps, audit findings, and the audit report in accordance with IAG policies and procedures
Guide team on how to validate and execute corrective actions / Management Action Plans (MAPs) are impactful, sustainable, and improve the control environment of the business unit
Support business monitoring activities with audit leadership, tracking key metrics to identify control issues and trends; stay up to date with evolving industry trends, external news and regulatory changes, and analyze the impact to the business exams
Delegate tasks to team members; guide Senior/Staff in assessing risks, evaluating control design, and executing audit tests; review and provide feedback on work papers
Serve as a People Leader, providing mentorship, coaching, and career development support for direct reports
Effectively coach, teach, mentor, and develop less experienced colleagues and co-sourced resources in geographically diverse locations across all aspects of their role, the audit and analytic lifecycle, audit methodology and best practices
Conduct post-audit feedback discussions with audit team members to provide actionable feedback, support development, and recognize accomplishments
Guide team to proactively and routinely communicate task status, roadblocks, challenges, suggesting potential solutions to the team
Begin to develop subject matter expertise in a specific line of business
Serve as the first level of escalation, effectively navigating problems and difficult conversations
Attend report / issue conversations with management, work with Director / Team Leader to communicate and action on next steps
Report on assigned tasks in client reporting meetings; assist with preparing materials for Regulatory exams
Follow-up with management to ensure management action plans are closed effectively and timely

Qualifications

Minimum Qualifications

6+ years of audit experience
Prior experience working at a Big Four / G-SIB
Demonstrates strong written and verbal communication skills to deliver deliverables with quality, and actionable value-add feedback to management on issues, opportunity areas, and deficiency solutions
Effectively leads a team in a fast-paced environment to drive business results, utilizing related project management skills, employing creative thinking, and the ability to work on competing priorities
Applies critical thinking to break-down complex problems into components, and solve using data analysis, process, risk control knowledge, and experience to drive risk-based conclusions and decisions
Applies control theory and professional auditing practices throughout the audit lifecycle
Understands regulations, regulatory risks, accounting, and financial industry best practices relevant to the business, including emerging technology and data considerations, and incorporates into the audit approach to enhance outcomes
Experience with technology control testing including automated processing, interface inputs, reports, application security, business continuity and third parties

Preferred Qualifications

Experience with data analytic tools, data visualization, key risk indicators (KRIs), key performance indicators (KPIs), information systems / technology, and scorecards / dashboards, etc.
Interest in working with data, interpreting results, analytic best practices and experience with data analytics tools and data visualization
Professional certification: CISA, CPA, CIA, CISM, CISSP or other technology-focused certification.

Employment eligibility to work with American Express in the United States is required as the company will not pursue visa sponsorship for these positions.

About Us

At American Express, our culture is built on a 175-year history of innovation, shared values and Leadership Behaviors, and an unwavering commitment to back our customers, communities, and colleagues. From delivering differentiated products to providing world-class customer service, we operate with a strong risk mindset, ensuring we continue to uphold our brand promise of trust, security, and service.

As part of Team Amex, you’ll experience our powerful backing with comprehensive support for your holistic well-being and many opportunities to learn new skills, develop as a leader, and grow your career. Here, your voice and ideas matter, your work makes an impact, and together, you will help us define the future of American Express.

About The Team

We back you with benefits that support your holistic well-being so you can be and deliver your best. This means caring for you and your loved ones' physical, financial, and mental health, as well as providing the flexibility you need to thrive personally and professionally:

Competitive base salaries
Bonus incentives
6% Company Match on retirement savings plan
Free financial coaching and financial well-being support
Comprehensive medical, dental, vision, life insurance, and disability benefits
Flexible working model with hybrid, onsite or virtual arrangements depending on role and business need

jobs.title: Director of Information Technology
jobs.description:
📍 New Jersey, USA (Onsite)
💰 Competitive Salary + Bonus + Benefits

Are you an experienced IT leader looking for an opportunity to shape technology strategy within a growing pharmaceutical organisation?

Our client is seeking an IT Director to lead technology, digital transformation, compliance, and business systems across the organization. This is an excellent opportunity for someone who thrives in a hands-on leadership role, enjoys working closely with executive stakeholders, and has experience supporting growth within a regulated Life Sciences environment.

The successful candidate will bring strong Pharmaceutical or broader Life Sciences experience, a solid understanding of GxP-regulated environments, and a track record of implementing scalable technology solutions that support business growth.

The Opportunity

As IT Director, you will be responsible for developing and executing the company's technology strategy while ensuring all systems remain secure, compliant, reliable, and aligned with business objectives.

You will partner with leaders across Quality, Manufacturing, Supply Chain, Regulatory Affairs, Clinical, and Commercial functions to drive operational excellence and support the company's continued growth.

Key Responsibilities

Develop and execute the company's IT and Digital Strategy.
Provide leadership across infrastructure, applications, cybersecurity, and business systems.
Ensure compliance with GxP, FDA, 21 CFR Part 11, Data Integrity, and industry regulatory requirements.
Own IT governance, risk management, and cybersecurity initiatives.
Lead Computer System Validation (CSV) and system compliance activities.
Manage and develop relationships with technology vendors and service providers.
Partner with senior leadership to support business growth and transformation.
Oversee ERP, Quality, Manufacturing, Laboratory, and commercial business systems.
Establish scalable processes, policies, and controls appropriate for a growing pharmaceutical company.
Build and manage technology budgets and roadmaps.
Drive digital transformation and automation initiatives across the organisation.
Ensure business continuity, disaster recovery, and data protection measures are maintained.

Required Experience

✅ Experience within Pharmaceutical, Biotechnology, Medical Device, or other regulated Life Sciences organisations.
✅ Previous experience in an IT Director, Head of IT, IT Manager, or senior technology leadership position.
✅ Strong knowledge of:
GxP regulations
Computer System Validation (CSV)
FDA-regulated environments
21 CFR Part 11
Data Integrity requirements
Quality Management Systems
✅ Experience working within smaller, growing pharmaceutical or biotech companies where flexibility and hands-on leadership are required.
✅ Experience supporting:
Manufacturing operations
Quality systems
ERP platforms
Business applications
Infrastructure and cybersecurity environments
✅ Excellent stakeholder management and communication skills.
